legend_summary: Parvati asked Shiva why he wore a garland of skulls and how he alone was deathless. He agreed to tell her the Amar Katha, the secret of immortality, but only where no living being could hear. On the way he shed his bull Nandi at Pahalgam, the moon at Chandanwari, his snakes at Sheshnag, Ganesha at Mahagunas and the five elements at Panchtarni. Inside the cave a pair of pigeons, hidden under the deer-skin, overheard and became immortal; pilgrims still look for them. Folklore credits the shepherd Buta Malik with rediscovering the cave after a sadhu's gift of coal turned to gold. The ice lingam forms naturally.

legend_summary: The goddess took birth as Vaishnavi, uniting the powers of Kali, Lakshmi and Saraswati. Lord Rama asked her to wait in the Trikuta hills until his Kalki form. When the tantric Bhairon Nath pursued her, she shot an arrow to create the Banganga stream, rested at Charan Paduka and meditated nine months in the narrow Ardhkuwari (Garbh Joon) cave. At the holy cave she took the form of Mahakali and beheaded him; his head fell on the hill where Bhairon temple stands. Forgiving him, she ruled that the yatra is complete only after visiting Bhairon.
